column2: Due to the ongoing pandemic, the 2020 Thanksgiving Retreat took place at the monastery while retreatants particpated via Zoom and Youtube. Unfortunately the YouTube recordings have frequent audio and video freezes, and only the first three Q&A sessions are useable.

column6: Session title
Text

Three questions about working with intense emotions:
1) Whenever I am unhappy or even have an intense feeling of sadness, my mind thinks that it is okay. Sadness is there, I even cry sometimes, but then eventually that feeling of sadness goes away. Why do I feel it is okay to be sad sometimes? Is it okay to feel this way?
2) I would appreciate any tips or guidance on working with deep anger or rage and other-blaming, specifically around working with recent traumatic events. These seem to be where the feelings are coming from, and it's easy for the mind to spin out for a long time on them.
3) How should I deal with difficult emotions during meditation like anxiety and sadness? Also, how do I deal with anxiety throughout the day?
AN 3.100: Salt in the River Ganges.

When I practice with you guys in the Ajahn Chah tradition, the flavor the Buddha is revered feels different from other, more Western teaching I have encountered. When referring to the Three Jewels, the Buddha seems to be referred to exclusively as the historical Buddha at Abhayagiri, as opposed to also including the Buddha-nature within all people and our own potential for enlightenment. Can you speak to that a bit? Also, although I am very happy to revere the Buddha, the way he is referred to in the chants seems like idolization, making into our God. Any advice with how I might work with the feeling of discomfort around that?
Homage to the Buddha, Chanting Book p. 4.
How should we practice with the second Enlightenment Factor of dhammavicaya, investigation of dhammas?
MN 10.36-45: Mindfulness of dhammas.
Must one attain jhāna or samādhi before one can practice the second, third, and fourth Foundations of Mindfulness in the satipaṭṭhāna?

Can we really let go of personality and live through the Four Noble Truths as Ajahn Pasanno explained this morning? At times I come close, but then fear sets in and sounds like this: 'Nope, you have three teenagers and this kind of spiritual bypass will not help you navigate the real world.' I yearn to jump over that chasm, but fear and doubt hold me back.

My mom and her siblings may have mental health issues. The live in a place where mental [illness] is a taboo, professional help is limited and hard to access. She is 77 years old. At times she can get very quick, smart, aggressive, super energetic, and destructive. Other times she can be dark, depressed, stay up in the night, tired in the day. Right now my dad (78 years old) is the only person who can handle her and take care of her. I worry when my dad is gone, no one is going to be able to handle her. I find this overwhelming. I spend a lot of time dwelling on this issue. How do I approach this?
Ud 3.10: "However they conceive of it, it is always other than that."
Ajahn Karuṇadhammo's father asks him to write down his worries and review them at the end of the day.

What is the correspondence between the Four Foundations of Mindfulness and the Five Aggregates? Obviously feeling is feeling, but what are body, mind, and dhamma? Is mindfulness of the body mindfulness of form or mindfulness of sense consciousness?
MN 10.4-31: Mindfulness of the body; MN 10.36-45: Mindfulness of dhammas.
The meaning of ajahn and krooba ajahn.
Please give me an example of samādhi, sati, and sampajañña.

How to harness discursive thinking throughout the day to aid one's practice? I have not been reading recently and have not had to do much of anything that is intellectually challenging, so on the rare occasions I make an effort to use this faculty, it is a bit clunky and imprecise. Are there techniques that have worked for you for keeping the thinking mind sharp and supportive such as reflecting and investigating while doing tasks, reading and writing about Dhamma themes, etc.?
MN 10.4: Simile of a skilled wood turner.

During meditation I sometimes feel a sense of tightness in the body. When I pay attention to that tightness, there is a feeling of loneliness or sadness associated with it. Should I stay focused on that sensation until it is gone or another technique you recommend?
Are sati and the Unconditioned the same?
For the eighth of the Eight Precepts, can I use a sleeping pad? The floor is really cold at night.
What should I do if I feel drowsy during sitting meditation?
AN 7.61: Mahāmoggallāna is nodding.

I feel like I care about something, say someone's health. If I sincerely care, then I must want them to get better, but is this a form of attachment? I have no control over the outcome, but if I say, 'I hope you get well soon,' irt seems hollow or just words if I am not somehow attached or have a desire for the outcome to be positive.

During one sitting, do I stay with one meditation object or can I switch to others? For example, from focus on the breath switch to contemplation of the body, contemplation of death, or lovingkindness.

As I was walking, I focused on the body aspect of Right Mindfulness, and then the mind would appear and its contents would capture my attention. I tried going back to the body contemplation and realized that the mind is here too and its content here. Maybe I should contemplate these other frames of reference. I noticed that the half-hour walk was going between these three aspects. Do you recommend that we work on the body and only the body at one sitting and others another or is it fruitful to work on whatever arises?
Holding a bird.|Ajahn Chah
MN 43.9: Conjoined not disjoined.
Would you please give us a little background and philosophy of Chi Gong? How is it helpful to the body?
Expression of gratitude for the 2020 Thanksgiving Retreat.

I take part in support groups for relatives of those who are dependent on intoxicating substances. I take time away from Dhamma activities to participate in the groups and also to be of service to those who are still suffering. Sometimes I feel guilty about that.
AN 8.39: Keeping the Five Precepts benefits oneself and others.
We are three friends coming together in the same house to be a part of the retreat. Is there any advice you could give us?
When an enlightened being dies, his body goes back to nature and that's it. Nothing else happens? I don't understand what gets reborn in a non-enlightened being.
SN 22.86: The quadrilemma.
SN 12.64.8: Light that doesn't land.
What would you suggest one does when one feels so down one doesn't want to do anything?

When around people who are pursuing things like fame or wealth or act in wrong ways, I find myself judging them. I often find myself disconnected from our society because of this. What would you suggest one do in such cases? It's difficult to find people I truly connect with.
Thank you for the spiritual deep cleaning. How does one move past the first and second jhāna? I seem to get stuck there for obvious reasons.
You Westerners should cultivate paññā and Right View first and then get into samādhi.|Ajahn Thoon Khippapañño

Could you explain why music is not viewed as a good thing in Buddhism? Music therapy has been very helpful, and I feel that listening to music helps me stay present and clears my mind as if it helped stop thoughts coming in.

In the Four Right Efforts, I understand preventing unwholesome states from arising and encouraging the arising of wholesome states to mean cultivating conditions conducive to the latter and not the former as opposed to somehow emotionally suppressing unwholesome states. I'm thinking about what Ajahn Sumedho says about allowing states to arise and cease rather than suppressing them. Does this seem right and useful?

When the Buddha talks about the Four Establishments of Mindfulness and how one remains focused on the mind in and of itself, what is the object of the mind? Is the direct attention to the physical brain for breathing in and breathing out? When I try to remain focused on the heart, I could sense the feeling of gladness. Is that the mind or the feeling?
How to cope with the pain and face boredom during meditation practice?
What is the difference between merit and pārami? Is pārami anicca? When we do something bad, does that lessen our pārami or is that its own separate process?
AN 4.77: Imponderables.
Should we strive to create meaning in our lives or accept that there is none? Well, I don't know if there is one.
If you hadn't become a monk, what do you think you'd be doing with your life right now? Do you sometimes think about this?

During walking meditation, I was immersing my attention into the body and sounds, particularly trying to experience consciousness. At one of these moments that sound hit my awareness, I zeroed in on experiencing the pure consciousness mechanism before sound hit it. It was very subtle. Immediately I felt an unpleasant feeling in my stomach that resembled fear. I got disconnected from it and was wondering why fear would show up, as if I was close to seeing something that the little me wasn't ready for. ... Is it possible to experience consciousness without its object? ...
DN 11.85 and MN 49.25: References to viññāṇaṃ anidassanaṃ.
SN 12.64.8: Light that doesn't land.

In addition to the path factors and other bodhipakkhiya dhammas, what are the most important qualities for monastics to develop to sustain the gradual training for the long term? Do these qualities differ in some respects form those that are essential for lay disciples to sustain long-term practice?
[Wings to Awakening]().
Please explain how self and world arises and passes away every moment due to causes and disappearance of causes. What are the best ways to experience this phenomena in daily living?
